items.name: Reedsport, Douglas County
items.note: The town nearest the events of 1828 and the base for the project. The July 2000 newspaper article that began the memorial project ran in The Reedsport Courier.

items.name: The mouth of the Smith River, where it enters the Umpqua
items.note: The general ground of the events of 14 July and 28 October 1828, as the creator’s own index describes it. The Library names the river mouth and nothing finer.

items.name: Bolon Island
items.note: The site on Highway 101 of the state historical marker for Jedediah Smith — the older stone marker and the panel that replaced it. The subject of the committee’s 2023 request to the Oregon Travel Information Council.

items.name: Fort Umpqua
items.note: The Hudson’s Bay Company post; a stop on the third day of the 2023 Rendezvous, with a tour script from the Elkton Community Education Center.

items.name: Fort Vancouver
items.note: Where Arthur Black arrived on 8 August 1828 and where the Rendezvous ended on 5 April 2023. Under construction during Smith’s winter there.

items.name: Coos History Museum
items.note: Visited on the second day of the Rendezvous for the Youst archive and McLeod’s history.

items.name: The Main Rock quarry, Kentuck Creek, near North Bend
items.note: Where the memorial stone was chosen and loaded in June 2023.

items.name: Champoeg
items.note: Fourth-day stop, and where the offer of the memorial stone was made on 4 April 2023.

items.name: Willamette Falls
items.note: Fourth-day stop; the Museum of the Oregon Territory.

items.name: Sunset Bay and Shore Acres
items.note: Camps of 5 and 6 July 1828, and second-day stops in 2023.

items.name: The Hollering Place
items.note: A local village site on Coos Bay, and a stop on the second day of the Rendezvous. Named as the creator names it; the Library adds nothing about it.

items.name: Harris Beach
items.note: A second-day stop in 2023, photographed by Peter Meyerhof; the creator uses it to show what the 1700 Cascadia earthquake left for the party to cross.

items.name: Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, California
Wamic, Creswell, Corvallis, Roseburg, Eugene and Cottage Grove
items.note: The Oregon towns where the plaque, the sign artwork, the engraving, the county permissions and the printing were done, as the project’s own sponsor list records them.
